original_question: For the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs, where one must cover every point of the graph by radius-r balls centered anywhere on the graph, what is the complexity when r is an algebraic real number? More specifically, if r is algebraic and not a unit fraction, must the problem be NP-hard?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2 ("Vertex cover"), specifically the unnumbered paragraph under "Discretization, tractability and r-certificates" that asks about the complexity of the continuous minimum r-cover problem for algebraic real radii and records Hartmann et al.'s conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct problem family: the continuous counterpart of minimum vertex cover, namely covering every point of a continuous graph by radius-r balls whose centers may lie anywhere on the graph. It also correctly targets the exact unresolved complexity regime singled out in the paper: fixed algebraic real radii r, especially the conjectured NP-hardness when r is not a unit fraction.
missing_details: The paper's problem is defined on continuous graphs in the sense of Definitions 1–4: a finite endpoint set with unit-length continuous edges, equipped with the shortest-path metric.
A ball must be understood in the paper's metric-graph sense (Definition 8), not as a Euclidean ball in an ambient space.
The radius r is a fixed positive algebraic real constant; it is not part of the input instance.
To make the complexity question stand-alone, it should be phrased via the decision problem: given a continuous graph G and an integer k, does G admit an r-cover of size at most k?

The paper's nearby context states the known dichotomy for rational radii: for every rational r the problem is in NP; it is polynomial-time solvable for unit fractions and NP-hard for rational non-unit fractions.
The phrase "unit fraction" should be spelled out explicitly in a stand-alone version as "of the form 1/q for some positive integer q."
The paper frames this as an open problem / conjecture, not as an already proved hardness theorem.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are metric-graph assumptions instead.
refined_question: Fix a positive algebraic real number r. Let G be a continuous graph with unit-length edges, endowed with its shortest-path metric, and let an r-cover of G mean a family of radius-r balls, centered at arbitrary points of G, whose union contains every point of G. What is the computational complexity of the decision problem "given G and k, does G admit an r-cover of size at most k?" In particular, is this problem NP-hard for every fixed algebraic real r that is not a unit fraction, i.e. not of the form 1/q for any positive integer q?
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft. Definition 10 gives exactly the continuous minimum r-cover problem, and the paragraph "Discretization, tractability and r-certificates" is the only place in the paper that isolates the algebraic-radius complexity question. That paragraph also states the surrounding rational-radius results and then formulates the precise conjectural extension to algebraic radii. I therefore kept the question narrowly on fixed algebraic r for general continuous graphs, without drifting into duality, approximation, or other sections.
